points: The Q3 2026 (ending Sept. 30) print will show whether the record 58 competitive core wins from FY26 — including 14 institutions with over $1 billion in assets — are converting into implementation revenue and ongoing processing fees.

It will reveal if processing revenue momentum carried forward: Q4 card revenue grew 5.4% and Jack Henry digital/transaction revenue grew 8.6%, and the long case needs that trend to support the 9.1% FY1 EPS growth consensus.
Reports suggest management issued FY2027 guidance with the Q4 release; the November call will be the first test of whether the company is tracking toward the $7.23 FY1 and $7.84 FY2 EPS consensus.

Q4 showed a margin divergence — GAAP operating income fell 12.2% and non-GAAP adjusted operating income fell 3.1% despite revenue growth — so the next print must show whether operating leverage is stabilizing or re-expanding.

The balance sheet and capital deployment picture matters: Q4 buybacks were $164 million at $140 and cash fell to $12.1 million, so the print will show whether cash generation supports continued repurchases without crimping growth investment.

At a forward P/E of ~23.5x and PEG of ~2.6x, the stock is priced for sustained execution; the print and any guidance refresh must confirm ~9% annual EPS growth to justify the premium versus the theme median.
Peer prints from TOST, PAYO, and EVTC in early November will offer sector context, but JKHY’s own core-win conversion and processing revenue growth are the decisive read-throughs for the long.
watch: Adjusted revenue growth holds or reaccelerates versus the FY26 full-year 7.3% pace — supports the long.
Processing/card revenue and digital/transaction revenue stay positive and maintain mid-to-high single-digit growth — supports the long.
Operating income margin stabilizes or expands after the Q4 contraction — supports the long.
FY2027 guidance and execution track toward FY1 EPS of $7.23 and FY2 EPS of $7.84 — supports the long.
